answer.rationale: Hard expiry in 14 days, 94% line utilization, and no buffer make delivery risk the binding constraint. Switching primary or deferring a non-auto-renewing contract would raise interruption risk; adding a second source does not replace the expiring primary in the one action available. c4 says benchmarking at renewal moved the incumbent on price and terms, so the low-cost quote that already meets the 18% cut is leverage to pursue the spend mandate without a migration. c1 supports keeping incumbent integration. c2 is treated only as analogical cost evidence pending archive check—not as a go-ahead to cut over with zero buffer. Negotiation outcome and whether the incumbent can actually hit 18% remain uncertain.
